questions.question: Why do writers use literary devices?
options: To create imagery, evoke emotion and add layers of meaning
To make texts longer
Because school curricula require them
To confuse readers deliberately
questions.explanation: Literary devices create vivid imagery, evoke emotional responses, convey complex ideas and make language memorable.

questions.question: What is the key principle when analysing a literary device in a text?
options: Explain its effect on the reader, not just identify it
List as many devices as possible
Assume every device means the same thing
Ignore the context
questions.explanation: Good analysis connects technique to effect: not just naming the device, but explaining what it does in context.

questions.question: How do skilled writers use literary devices?
options: Purposefully, often with several devices working together
Randomly, for decoration
Only in the first paragraph
Only in poetry, never in prose
questions.explanation: Good writers use devices deliberately, and multiple devices often work together to build meaning.

questions.question: Why can the same literary device have different effects in different texts?
options: Because context shapes how a device works and what it means
Because devices change their definitions every year
Because readers cannot recognise devices
It cannot — a device always has one effect
questions.explanation: Context matters: repetition might build tension in one text and comfort in another.

questions.question: Which benefit comes from understanding literary devices?
options: Deeper reading, better analysis and improved writing
Faster reading speed only
No need to read whole texts
Automatic exam success
questions.explanation: Understanding devices lets you see beneath the surface, write insightful analyses and use the techniques yourself.
